new_evidence.primary_source: Hydra: Efficient, Correct Code Generation via Checkpoint-and-Rollback Support, arXiv:2605.15238v1
new_evidence.material_update: Hydra explicitly holds checker implementation, checkpoint interval, prompts, and sampling configuration fixed while baseline rollback policies differ in rollback-node selection after an error. On 100 initially failing C++ tasks from Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, TokPol is reported to have substantially lower latency and token consumption than Random, Backwards, and Entropy. This partially resolves the target-selector gap for static compiler-error recovery, but retry-memory/attempt details are not literally identical and the selector ablation is efficiency-centric rather than a general-agent final-success comparison.
new_evidence.scope_guard: Do not generalize beyond static C/C++ compiler-error recovery; do not attribute overall Hydra 71% latency/70% token reductions solely to target selection; do not invent exact Figure-7 quantiles.
